## Lockable fridge for offices and share houses

In an office kitchen or a share house, a lockable fridge stops arguments about whose food is whose. A compact fridge with a lock in a bedroom or private study keeps your own items secure while the main kitchen fridge stays shared. Agree who holds the key and where the spare is kept. If the fridge is in a common area, a clear label saying it is locked helps everyone understand the rule.

## Lockable fridges for shops, cafes and function rooms

Shops and cafes often keep high-value or age-restricted stock in a lockable fridge so that only staff can open it. Function rooms and clubs use a locking bar fridge to secure stock between events. A lockable glass door fridge lets customers see the product without being able to take it. Check that the lock suits the volume of staff access you need, because a stiff lock slows service.

## Maintenance and replacement

Keys get lost and locks wear, so keep a spare key and check the lock occasionally. A little lubricant suited to locks keeps the barrel turning, but keep it away from the door seal. If a lock fails, a replacement fridge door lock is often available, and our [spare parts](/accessories-parts/spare-parts/) category lists common items. Replace worn seals promptly so the door stays tight.

## What to do if the key is lost

Contact the supplier with the model number to ask about replacement keys or locks. Do not force the lock, because you may damage the door or the seal. Keep a record of the model and serial number alongside the receipt for easy reference.

## Running costs and energy use

A mini bar fridge is small, but it runs all day. Thermoelectric models can use more power for their size than compressor models, and a unit in a hot room works harder. Compare the energy information on the product page, keep the unit out of the sun and avoid opening the door more than you need. A compact bar fridge in a cool, ventilated spot is usually the most economical.

## Cleaning and care

Wipe the interior regularly, clean up spills straight away and check the door seal. Defrost any freezer box as the manual describes. Leave the door ajar if the fridge is switched off for a long time so odours do not build up. Keep the vents clear of dust.

## Moving and carrying

A mini bar fridge is easy to move, but let it stand upright for the time recommended in the manual before you switch it on after transport. Empty it before moving, and secure the door so it does not swing open. Our [delivery information](/delivery/) explains how orders are sent to you.

insert:
## Matching a black fridge to the room

Black looks best when it matches the rest of the room. Pair it with dark timber, black tapware and warm lighting for a moody bar, or with white and timber for contrast. Check the handle colour and trim, because chrome and black handles create different looks. If you are buying several appliances, choose finishes that sit together rather than competing.

## Black bar fridge for venues

Bars, cocktail lounges and nightclubs often prefer black because it recedes into the background and lets the lighting and the bottles stand out. In a commercial setting, wipe-clean surfaces and durable coatings matter more than the shade. Our [cocktail bar page](/venues/cocktail-bars/) and [nightclub page](/venues/nightclubs/) show typical equipment for those venues.

## Brands that offer black finishes

Many makers offer black cabinets and glass door models. Tefcold, for example, is known for sleek black bar merchandisers, which you can view on our [brand page](/brands/tefcold/). Compare the warranty and build as well as the colour.

## Black fridge energy and heat

Colour does not change cooling performance, but a fridge in direct sun works harder. Keep any black fridge away from windows and heat sources, give it ventilation and keep the condenser clean. Those basics save more energy than the choice of finish.

## Seating, lighting and layout

A good home bar has a place to sit, a place to pour and a clear path to the fridge. Put the fridge within easy reach of the bar top so you do not walk across the room for each drink. Add warm lighting and a bench for glasses. Leave room for the fridge door to swing open fully. If space is tight, a sliding door or a reversible hinge helps.

## Planning a budget

A home bar fridge does not have to be the most expensive item in the room. Set a budget, decide which features matter and compare models in that range. A glass door and a lock add cost, so decide if they are needed. Our [cheap bar fridge guide](/guides/cheap-bar-fridge-australia-what-to-check/) lists checks for lower-priced models, and our [best bar fridge guide](/guides/best-bar-fridge-australia-how-to-choose/) lists what to compare.

## Games room and entertaining area use

A games room fridge sees heavy use during parties and little use in between. Make sure there is enough space to chill drinks quickly before guests arrive. A second fridge in the entertaining area, perhaps outdoors, spreads the load. Plan for ice too, and consider a small bar freezer.

## Maintenance

Clean the fridge regularly, check the seals and keep the vents clear. If the fridge is in a garage, dust builds up faster, so clean the condenser more often. A well-kept fridge lasts longer and runs better.

## Stock rotation and restocking

A back bar fridge works best when it is loaded in a consistent pattern. Place new stock behind older stock so the oldest drinks are served first, and keep like products together so staff can find them quickly. Restock outside peak times, and avoid loading a lot of warm bottles at once, because the fridge needs time to pull down the temperature.

## Cleaning and maintenance

Wipe the doors and shelves each day, clean the seals weekly and clear the condenser on a regular schedule. A dusty condenser forces the compressor to work harder and shortens life. Check hinges and sliding tracks, and clear spilled drinks straight away to avoid sticky tracks.

## Energy use in a busy bar

A back bar cooler runs for long hours, so energy use matters. Compare stated power consumption, check the quality of the seals and keep the unit away from heat sources. LED lighting runs cooler than older lighting, and glass doors with double glazing reduce heat gain.
